metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB.NET code-behind with ASP.NET WebForms entry point) present with database connections and CRUD operations. Single deployable unit on IIS 6. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: SQL Server database connections with INSERT and SELECT operations, user-specific session data (EmployeeId). Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.15 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (within 2-11 range) maps to Remediation Required tier. This occurs because 20 of 31 findings are Medium-severity (non-core questions scoring 1), pushing the overall score below 1.5 without generating enough High-severity findings to reach the >=12 threshold for Not Ready tier. The score-based Not Ready assessment is the more accurate characterization.

findings.title: Managed Compute — All compute on unsupported IIS 6 / Windows Server 2003
findings.description: All compute runs on a single IIS 6 server on Windows Server 2003 with .NET Framework 2.0. No managed compute services (ECS, EKS, Lambda, Fargate) are in use. Both the OS and web server are long past end of life.
findings.gap: No managed compute — entirely on unsupported, unpatchable on-premises infrastructure with no path to AWS managed services without a platform migration.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the application targeting modern .NET on managed compute (ECS/Fargate or Lambda behind API Gateway). Windows Server 2003 and IIS 6 cannot be migrated as-is.

findings.title: Managed Databases — Self-managed SQL Server 2005 on-premises
findings.description: Database is SQL Server 2005 running self-managed on-premises at IP 10.0.6.15. Connection via SqlClient with plaintext credentials in web.config. No managed database services in use.
findings.gap: Entirely self-managed database on an unsupported engine version with no automated failover, patching, or backup visible in repository.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server or Aurora PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS for data migration. Implement Secrets Manager for credential management.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — No orchestration services
findings.description: No workflow orchestration services (Step Functions, MWAA, Temporal) detected. All logic is inline sequential code with no orchestration.
findings.gap: No orchestration of any kind. No foundation for adding approval workflows or notification flows.
findings.recommendation: When modernizing, implement Step Functions for multi-step workflows (e.g., timesheet submission → manager approval → payroll notification).

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming — No messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure detected. All operations are synchronous HTTP with direct database writes. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Kafka, or RabbitMQ.
findings.gap: No messaging infrastructure. State changes are not published as events, preventing integration with downstream systems.
findings.recommendation: Implement EventBridge or SNS for timesheet state change events when modernizing.

findings.title: Network Security — No network controls or HTTPS
findings.description: No VPC, no security groups, no network segmentation. No HTTPS — Forms auth cookie sent in clear. Database accessed via IP on internal network with no encryption in transit.
findings.gap: No network security controls. No TLS/HTTPS. No network segmentation between web tier and database tier.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets, security groups enforcing least-privilege, TLS termination at load balancer, and encrypted database connections.

findings.title: API Entry Point — Direct service exposure with no gateway
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or any load balancer. Application exposed directly via IIS 6 with no intermediary.
findings.gap: Direct service exposure with no managed entry point. No throttling, no WAF, no DDoS protection.
findings.recommendation: Deploy behind API Gateway or ALB with WAF when modernizing.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — No auto-scaling, single static server
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Single IIS 6 server with fixed capacity. No ASG, no ECS service scaling, no Lambda concurrency.
findings.gap: Single server with no ability to scale. Complete single point of failure.
findings.recommendation: Deploy on auto-scaling compute (ECS with service auto-scaling or Lambda).

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — No backup configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. SQL Server 2005 database has no backup strategy documented or automated. No PITR, no retention policies.
findings.gap: No automated backups. Data loss from any failure event would be unrecoverable from repository evidence.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS which provides automated backups with configurable retention. Enable PITR.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — Zero IaC
findings.description: No infrastructure as code exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC files. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. No reproducibility, no version control of infrastructure state, no disaster recovery from code.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in IaC (Terraform or CDK). Start with compute and database resources.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No CI/CD pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual Visual Studio publish to a network share.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy process. All deployments are manual with no quality gates.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with build, test, and deploy stages. Add automated rollback on failure.

findings.title: Programming Languages — VB.NET on .NET Framework 2.0 (unsupported)
findings.description: VB.NET on .NET Framework 2.0 (released 2005). Runtime is completely unsupported. AWS SDK for .NET requires .NET Framework 4.5+ minimum. ASP.NET WebForms is deprecated.
findings.gap: Language/runtime has no AWS SDK support and no cloud-native tooling. Cannot use any modern AWS services without complete platform migration.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to modern .NET (8+) with C# and ASP.NET Core. This provides full AWS SDK support and cross-platform Linux deployment.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — Tightly-coupled monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled single-page WebForms monolith. Presentation, business logic, and data access all in single code-behind file. No module boundaries.
findings.gap: No architectural separation. Cannot extract, scale, or test any component independently. Pervasive shared state prevents decomposition without rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite with clean architecture separating API, business logic, and data access. Design as independent service with REST API surface.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — 100% synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. No async patterns, no background processing, no message publication on state changes.
findings.gap: 100% synchronous operations. State changes cannot notify downstream systems without synchronous coupling.
findings.recommendation: Implement async event publication for state changes (EventBridge/SNS). Use async/await for database operations.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — All operations synchronous
findings.description: All operations are synchronous regardless of duration. Unbounded SELECT query with no pagination will become long-running as data grows.
findings.gap: No async processing capability. No mechanism to handle operations exceeding request timeout.
findings.recommendation: Implement pagination for data retrieval. Add async job processing for batch operations.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — No versioning
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. Single WebForms page with no REST API surface. No URL, header, or query parameter versioning.
findings.gap: No versioning. Changes break existing behavior directly.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based versioning (e.g., /api/v1/timesheets) when modernizing to REST API.

findings.title: Service Discovery — Hard-coded database IP
findings.description: Database endpoint hard-coded as IP address (10.0.6.15) in web.config. No service discovery, no DNS resolution, no environment-variable indirection.
findings.gap: Hard-coded service endpoint. Cannot relocate database without modifying and redeploying configuration.
findings.recommendation: Use DNS-based service discovery or SSM Parameter Store for all service endpoints.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — No managed object storage
findings.description: No S3 or managed object storage. No unstructured data handling capabilities. Only structured SQL data storage.
findings.gap: No S3 or managed object storage. No document parsing pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Implement S3 for document/attachment storage needs when modernizing.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — Scattered inline SQL
findings.description: Database queries scattered directly in page code-behind using raw SqlClient with string concatenation. No repository pattern, no DAO layer, no ORM.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction. SQL queries directly in presentation layer. Cannot enforce data contracts.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern or Entity Framework Core when modernizing.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL — SQL Server 2005 (9+ years past EOL)
findings.description: SQL Server 2005 end of extended support was April 12, 2016. Engine unsupported for 9+ years. No security patches available.
findings.gap: Database engine 9+ years past EOL with known unpatched vulnerabilities. No path to updates without migration.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported engine immediately — RDS SQL Server 2019/2022 or Aurora PostgreSQL.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — No encryption
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. SQL Server 2005 does not support TDE. Employee PII stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: Zero encryption at rest. Employee data (PII) stored unencrypted. Engine migration is prerequisite for encryption.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS/Aurora which provides encryption at rest by default with KMS.

findings.title: API Authentication — Insecure Forms auth without SSL
findings.description: Forms authentication with requireSSL=false. Auth cookie transmitted in clear text over HTTP. No token-based auth.
findings.gap: Authentication cookie sent unencrypted. No token-based authentication. No per-request authorization validation.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT with Cognito. Enforce HTTPS on all endpoints.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — Standalone Forms auth
findings.description: Application manages own authentication via Forms auth (Login.aspx). No centralized IdP integration.
findings.gap: Standalone authentication. No SSO. No centralized access management.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Cognito or corporate AD) when modernizing.

findings.title: Secrets Management — Plaintext credentials in source control
findings.description: Plaintext database credentials in web.config: User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006!. Comment acknowledges no encryption.
findings.gap: Critical: Production credentials visible in version-controlled source. Anyone with repo access has database credentials.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate exposed credentials. Implement AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — Unpatchable OS
findings.description: Windows Server 2003 and IIS 6 past end of life (2015). No patching possible. No vulnerability scanning. No SSM Agent support.
findings.gap: Compute platform is unpatchable. Known unaddressed vulnerabilities in OS, web server, and runtime.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported compute — Fargate/Lambda eliminates OS patching, or ECS/EKS with Bottlerocket.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline for scanning to run in. Known SQL injection vulnerabilities exist undetected.
findings.gap: No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. Known SQL injection vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST and dependency scanning in CI/CD with blocking gates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — No tracing instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No tracing capability. Cannot trace requests or measure latency.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry or AWS X-Ray when modernizing.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency targets, no monitoring infrastructure.
findings.gap: No service level objectives. No monitoring to detect degradation.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for timesheet service (availability, latency). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business metrics tracking (timesheets submitted, hours logged).
findings.gap: No business-level visibility. Cannot determine if system delivers value.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom business metrics alongside infrastructure metrics when modernizing.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — No alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no incident management integration.
findings.gap: No proactive alerting. Failures detected only by user complaints.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for error rates and latency. Add anomaly detection.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No unit tests, no integration tests, no test frameworks.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No regression detection. Changes risk breaking functionality.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests for critical workflows. Add to CI pipeline as quality gate.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No observability exists
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no team attribution. Monitoring completely absent.
findings.gap: No observability ownership model. Monitoring is completely absent rather than merely unowned.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards, named alarm owners, and SLO definitions with team attribution.
